item.title: Comment on My excellent Conversation with Ross Douthat on God and religion by Ben G
item.description:
Ross's arguments in favor of religion being true are just as terrible as you'd expect.

He puts an utterly bizarre amount of credence on near-death experiences and "sightings" of angels, citing these as evidence of a God instead of using Occam's Razor and saying, "we know that people hallucinate, lie, and have delusions and mental disorders all the time, so that's probably what they are". It is so intellectually dishonest of him to count these in his favor so as to be devious.

He also hand-waves the question of "Why choose Catholicism and not be a Bayesian Deist since being a Catholic was just your inherited religion?" with a total lack of self-questioning. He essentially tells Tyler, "yea, but YOU believe in capitalism and libertarianism and those are culturally inherited for you well!" That is an insane response. A defender of capitalism can at least point to a couple hundreds years of statistics on mortality, freedom and GDP figures and say, "this is why capitalism is better than other economic systems" and have empirically verifiable reasons for their belief to debate.

Catholics can't point to ANYTHING to explain their enormous deviations from the Bible (Popes, etc.) other than tradition and inherited hierarchy. They don't even have their own holy book they can use as evidence! Yet Ross wants the world to take Catholicism as The Truth about metaphysics and the universe. This is insane.

I respect if you're religious and just proclaim your belief is based on pure faith, but to attempt these specious attempts at philosophy and reason as Ross does is just offensive and gives more ammo to the most irrational people in our culture and makes you realise that intellectualism is no guarantee of thinking critically.

The one saving grace of Ross new book is that every time these people try to defend their beliefs we see how thin their reasons really are.

item.title: Comment on My excellent Conversation with Ross Douthat on God and religion by Kevin
item.description:
It's frustrating how often people cite quantum mechanics as the justification for something, without really understanding it.

"In order for the ruler to be an instrument of measurement, you, Tyler Cowen, have to be perceiving it and be conscious of it."

Nope, that's just not how quantum mechanics works. An unconscious recording instrument will take measurements in exactly the same way that a conscious observer will. An entity cannot take quantum mechanical measurements to determine whether it is conscious or not. None of the interpretations of quantum mechanics differ on this.

I like Ross but he would be better off if he avoided citing quantum mechanics as evidence for anything.
